audits.mathematicalReason: Let angle B = b. Since AB = BC, angles BAC and ACB are equal, so both are 5b/2. Thus b + 5b/2 + 5b/2 = 180°, giving b = 30° and angle ACB = 75°. Vertical angles give angle DCE = 75°. Since CD = CE, the two remaining angles of triangle CDE are equal, so angle D = (180° − 75°)/2 = 52.5°. The assessed and support scopes match these steps.

audits.mathematicalReason: Write the screen dimensions as 4k by 3k inches. Its diagonal is 5k by the Pythagorean theorem, so k = 27/5 = 5.4. The width is therefore 21.6 inches and the height is 16.2 inches. The full-width 2:1 movie has height 10.8 inches, leaving two equal strips, each (16.2 − 10.8)/2 = 2.7 inches high. Both practical proportions and an application of the Pythagorean theorem are directly exercised.

figureEvidence.fact: The movie occupies the full screen width, with horizontal darkened strips above and below it and no side strips.

routes.label: Complete a square and remove corners

audits.mathematicalReason: Let the octagon's side length be s and its apothem be a. Eight central triangles give octagon area 8(sa/2) = 4sa. Rectangle ABEF has width s and height 2a, so its area is 2sa, exactly half the octagon's area. The square-corner route is also valid: the regular octagon has 135° interior angles, so completing its bounding square produces four 45°-45°-90° corner triangles with legs s/sqrt(2). The bounding square has side L = s(1 + sqrt(2)), and the octagon's area is L² − s² = 2s²(1 + sqrt(2)), twice the rectangle's area sL. These are alternative routes, not jointly required methods.

figureEvidence.fact: The vertices are labeled consecutively around the octagon. AB is the upper edge and FE is the opposite lower edge; these form the two opposite octagon sides used by rectangle ABEF.

audits.mathematicalReason: The indicated path consists of an outer quadrant arc, two inner quadrant arcs, two radial gaps, and an inner diameter. Their lengths total 10π + 5π + 5π + 10 + 10 + 20 = 20π + 40 meters. The result does not actually require assuming an unmarked right angle between the diameters: if the outer arc subtends α degrees, each inner arc subtends 180° − α, so their combined length is 20πα/180 + 2·10π(180 − α)/180 = 20π. Segment addition and subtraction account for the remaining 40 meters.

figureEvidence.fact: The arrows indicate travel from A around the upper-left outer arc, inward along the left radius, around the lower-left inner arc, up the inner diameter, around the upper-right inner arc, and outward along the right radius to K.
The left and right radial portions lie on one diameter, while the top and bottom inner-circle endpoints lie on another diameter through the common center.

audits.mathematicalReason: The displayed squares have side lengths 1, 2, and 3 tiles. With each successive side increasing by one tile, the sixth and seventh squares contain 6² = 36 and 7² = 49 tiles. The difference is 49 − 36 = 13 tiles. Recognizing the numerical pattern in the figures and calculating square areas are both defensible assessed scopes.

figureEvidence.fact: The first three figures are a single tile, a 2-by-2 tile square, and a 3-by-3 tile square.

audits.mathematicalReason: Triangle ABC has area 49sqrt(3). The hexagon consists of ABC and triangles ADB, BEC, CFA, which are congruent by the configuration's 120° rotational symmetry. Each added triangle therefore has area (91sqrt(3) − 49sqrt(3))/3 = 14sqrt(3), giving D a perpendicular distance 2sqrt(3) below AB. Put the common center at the origin, with A = (−7, −7sqrt(3)/3) and B = (7, −7sqrt(3)/3). The circumradius satisfies R² = 196/3, and D has y-coordinate −13sqrt(3)/3. Thus x_D² = 9; the depicted rotation and 0 < θ < 60° select x_D = −3. For the distance route, line OA is x − sqrt(3)y = 0, so D's distance to it is 5. The right triangle formed by the perpendicular foot has adjacent length sqrt(R² − 25) = 11sqrt(3)/3, yielding tan θ = 5sqrt(3)/11. Alternatively, OA·OD divided by R² gives cos θ = 11/14. Since θ is acute, sin θ = 5sqrt(3)/14, giving the same tangent. Both listed routes are valid alternatives.

figureEvidence.fact: The outer boundary follows A-D-B-E-C-F-A. The segments AB, BC, and CA divide this hexagon into triangle ABC and the three added triangles ADB, BEC, and CFA.
D lies outside ABC across AB, E across BC, and F across CA. Their placement identifies the rotation orientation used in the coordinate calculation; no angle or length is measured from the drawing.

audits.mathematicalReason: Each semicircle has diameter 2/π and radius 1/π, so each boundary arc has length π(1/π) = 1. There are four such arcs, giving perimeter 4. The square's sides are internal seams and do not contribute. The arc-length scope directly covers this computation.

figureEvidence.fact: One outward semicircle is constructed on each side of the square. The region's exterior boundary consists of the four semicircular arcs; the square's sides lie inside the region.

audits.mathematicalReason: Classify the white king's square. At each of the four corners it attacks three squares, leaving 9 − 1 − 3 = 5 choices for the black king. At each of the four noncorner edge squares it attacks five squares, leaving 3 choices. At the center it leaves no choices. Since the kings are distinguishable, the total is 4·5 + 4·3 + 1·0 = 32, with no division by two. This uses multiplication within each case and addition across disjoint cases, exactly matching the candidate scope.

figureEvidence.fact: The figure is a 3-by-3 grid with a king in the center and arrows to all eight surrounding squares, illustrating horizontal, vertical, and diagonal one-step attacks.
